emma_sales: Hey team — Sanjay from Aurora Health is asking about our Private deployment network constraints before signing the PO. Key asks: mutual TLS to the connector, preserve client source IPs for audit logs, and ability to route traffic from their on‑prem through a PrivateLink endpoint in a different AWS account. Can we confirm feasibility and any pricing impacts?

jordan_soleng: Short answer: feasible. Need to call out two things: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoints) terminates TLS at our ENI in the customer's VPC — mTLS to the connector is supported if the customer performs client cert auth to the endpoint, but we usually terminate TLS at our side too. 2) Source IP preservation across PrivateLink isn't preserved by default because traffic hits our ENI, you'll see the ENI IP as source. If they need original IP in app logs, we can pass X-Forwarded-For headers from our proxy or use a TCP tunnel option (transit VPN/Direct Connect) to preserve original src IPs.

mike_netops: Adding: we can support mTLS between customer and our connector if they upload their CA to the connector's trust store (or we do mTLS validation on a termination proxy). For source IP: PrivateLink = No native client srcip passthrough. Options: 
- Use ALB/NLB with proxy protocol and have connector log XFF.
- Use a dedicated Transit/VPN path to an instance that preserves src IPs.
- Or have their edge NAT translation map to a dedicated set of egress IPs (so audit maps to a stable set).

sanjay_customer: Hmm — audit team requires the actual originating IP per request (not just a static egress IP). They also require mutual auth for each TCP session. Would the proxy approach break mTLS?

jordan_soleng: Good question. Two patterns: 
1) Terminate mTLS at an ingress proxy we manage, proxy then mTLS (or mTLS-disabled TLS) upstream to the connector. That means the proxy can add XFF with the original IP. That satisfies logs but shifts mutual auth boundary to the proxy.
2) Use a layer 2/3 path (Direct Connect or site‑to‑site VPN) into the same VPC as our connector or into a transit VPC where we host the connector. Then client src IP is preserved and mTLS happens end-to-end. But that's heavier and usually part of a Dedicated/Private deployment pricing addendum.

emma_sales: Pricing question from procurement: how much more for the Direct Connect route vs PrivateLink only? Need a ballpark for the quote.

mike_netops: Ballpark: PrivateLink + standard Private deployment = baseline. Adding a managed VPN endpoint (we host a VPN gateway peer) + routing config = +20% monthly infra fee. Direct Connect assistance (dedicated circuit onboarding support, cross-connect coordination) = one‑time services fee + +35% monthly depending on port speed because of reserved bandwidth. I'll flag finance for exact numbers.

legal_bot: Security questionnaire update: "Can Redwood preserve originating client IPs for audit logs?" Proposed answer: "Yes — when using a routed/peered network path (VPN/Direct Connect to the Private deployment/transit VPC) or a proxy configured to forward X-Forwarded-For. PrivateLink interface endpoints do not preserve L3 source IPs."

jordan_soleng: I'll paste a sample snippet we can give their security team: 
```
Network options to preserve originating IPs:\n1) Site-to-Site VPN / Direct Connect into the customer's transit VPC (or into a dedicated VPC where the connector is deployed). This preserves layer 3 client source IPs end-to-end.
2) Configure our ingress proxy (managed by Redwood) to terminate mTLS and forward `X-Forwarded-For`/`True-Client-IP` headers to your application. Ensure TLS client cert validation is performed at the proxy.
3) If using PrivateLink, configure a stable egress IP pool on the customer side and map audit logs to that pool.
```

sanjay_customer: That snippet helps. For option 2, is the proxy a single AZ point of failure? We need HA and cert rotation processes documented.

mike_netops: Our managed proxy is deployed across multiple AZs in the region by default for Private deployments. Cert rotation: we support automatic rotation via the connector control plane; customer-provided client cert rotation can be automated via SCEP or uploaded via API. We'll include an SLA note.

emma_sales: Next steps for the deal: 1) Jordan — prepare short network architecture diagram showing PrivateLink vs VPN option and callouts for mTLS and src IP. 2) Mike — give a written pricing delta for managed VPN and Direct Connect assistance. 3) Legal — include the answer in the security questionnaire doc and add the cert rotation note. 4) Sanjay — confirm which option they prefer by EOD Thursday.

jordan_soleng: Working on the diagram now, posting a quick ASCII draft: 
```
CustomerOnPrem --[S2S VPN or DX]--> TransitVPC (customer) ---BGP---> Redwood Transit VPC (connector)
OR
CustomerOnPrem --[PrivateLink ENI in cust VPC]--> Redwood ENI (terminates TLS) --> Managed Proxy --> Connector
```

sanjay_customer: Appreciate the clarity. One more ask: can Redwood support client certificate revocation checking (CRL/OCSP) on the mTLS path?

mike_netops: Yes, we support OCSP stapling and CRL checks at the proxy/termination layer. If you need OCSP to a private OCSP responder, we'll need peering/VPN connectivity from our proxy to that OCSP endpoint or a signed transport path.

emma_sales: Great. I'll bundle this into the PO addendum. Jordan — can you drop the diagram + 1‑pager in the shared drive and ping me when done? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: New doc uploaded: /shared/aurora-health/network-options-2026-03-23.pdf (uploader: jordan_soleng)

jordan_soleng: Uploaded. Link sent via DM. Will draft the SOW text for the Direct Connect assist and managed VPN fee tonight.

sanjay_customer: Thanks everyone — we should be ready to sign after we review the SOW and the updated security questionnaire answers.

emma_sales: Awesome, keeping this thread open for any follow ups. :white_check_mark:
